sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section gives the precise time of the maamar: the eve of Sukkot 5739.

translations.translation: The eve of the holiday of Sukkot, 5739*

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the Midrashic interpretation of "the first day" regarding the four species, linking it to a new accounting after Yom Kippur.

translations.translation: "And you shall take for yourselves on the first day..."1
And it is brought in the Midrash2:
"Is it the first? Is it not the fifteenth
[day]3
? Rather, it is the first
[it is]3
for the accounting of sins."
For on Yom Kippur, the Holy One, blessed be He, forgives Israel for everything4,
and from Yom Kippur5
until the holiday, all of Israel are occupied with mitzvos,
this one occupies himself with his sukkah and that one with his lulav,
and on the first day of the holiday, the Holy One, blessed be He, says to them, "Whoever went, went, and from here onward6
is the accounting."
And from this it is understood7,
that the mitzvah of taking the four species on the fifteenth of Tishrei is because it is the first for accounting.
And one must understand the connection of "first for accounting" to the taking of the four species.
And even more so, explanation is needed according to what is brought in the Midrash8,
"Israel and the nations of the world come before the Holy One, blessed be He, on Rosh Hashanah, and we do not know who is victorious,
but by the fact that Israel go out from before the Holy One, blessed be He, with their lulavim and esrogim in their hands, we know that Israel are the victors,
therefore Moshe warns Israel and says to them, 'And you shall take for yourselves...'"
That is to say,
that the mitzvah of taking the four species on the holiday of Sukkot comes as a continuation of the judgment of Rosh Hashanah,
and why does it say "And you shall take for yourselves on the first day,"
that the mitzvah of taking the four species on this day is
(not because it is the fifteenth day from Rosh Hashanah,
but rather)
because on it a new matter begins,
"first for accounting."
